h1: UGC Video Ads for the Industry You Sell In
eyebrow: Find the Ad for Your Product
lead: Open the industry that matches what you sell, and turn one photo into a UGC ad. You already have the photo.

AI images for small online shops
intro: Open the category of the item you have. That page shows the moment shoppers use to decide, then you make a photo or a video from one picture. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600.
A video can include a script, an AI avatar, a voiceover or captions, and a track from the music library. Send it to TikTok, Facebook, or Instagram, or download the file.

faq.q: Why do creator-style ads tend to get watched?
faq.a: Shoppers stay when the clip feels like advice from someone who uses the item. For a blender, show the lid in the first second and the smoothie before you mention the blades.

faq.q: What does AI UGC mean for a shop ad?
faq.a: AI UGC means a product clip that looks like a creator made it. An AI avatar says a line you wrote, and you did not book a film crew to get that clip.

faq.q: Do I have to film something before I choose a plan?
faq.a: No. You choose a plan first. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600.

faq.q: How long does a UGC ad take to make?
faq.a: It does not take a shoot day. You review the file in your account after you submit the job.

faq.q: How do I make a UGC ad with an AI avatar?
faq.a: Open the category that matches the product, put an AI avatar on screen, and use a sentence you would print on the label. Export that file and load it in the ad account yourself.

faq.q: Where do the AI avatars for these ads come from?
faq.a: The AI avatars are part of AIVideosUGC. Open the actor library, pick a face, and that face can say the line you wrote.

faq.q: Can a listing URL become the whole video ad?
faq.a: Yes. A public face-oil page can supply the photo and the product name. The API is not required for a single file, and your shop software can still send that link.

faq.q: Do I need a creator's permission to run the ad?
faq.a: No. You can run the download as a paid ad for your own shop. The face was generated here, so there is no creator signature to collect.

faq.q: Can I change the video after it generates?
faq.a: Yes. If the sweater color is right and the sentence is wrong, change the sentence and run the job again.

faq.q: How is a filmed creator video unlike one made with an AI avatar?
faq.a: A filmed creator video puts a person you hired on camera. An AI avatar can take that role when a shop adds a new opening for the same kettle each week.

faq.q: Can an AI avatar stand in for a human creator?
faq.a: Yes, for the extra openings. If buyers already follow a specific founder, film that founder for the main spot. Use an AI avatar for the openings you would not hire out.

faq.q: How many languages can the avatar speak?
faq.a: As many as you can write accurately. A soap shop selling into Germany can type a German line and have an AI avatar speak it. A cloned voice needs a short sample you are allowed to use.

faq.q: Which languages can I write the line in?
faq.a: Whichever language is already on the listing. Just type the line in that language, and the actor speaks it.

faq.q: How quickly can I create a product ad?
faq.a: Paste the listing or the sentence, then review the file in your account. You do not wait on a shoot day.

faq.q: Can the avatar speak in a cloned voice?
faq.a: Yes. Give it a short sample from a speaker you are allowed to use. An AI avatar can say a new script in that voice on the next product.

faq.q: Can I make these ads without hiring a creator?
faq.a: Yes. If you already filmed the product yourself, use that clip and add a generated voice. If you only have a photo, an AI avatar can hold the item and speak.

faq.q: How is an AI UGC ad made?
faq.a: You supply the product photo and the sentence. The spoken line comes from that sentence, and an AI avatar delivers it in the language you typed.

faq.q: What kinds of product clips can I make?
faq.a: A recommendation, a how-to, an unboxing, or a review. A how-to can stop once the shirt is buttoned. You start from the photo you already have.

faq.q: What should I look for in a tool for this job?
faq.a: Judge the tool by whether one photo of your item can become a clip you would actually post. AIVideosUGC is built for that path.

faq.q: Which category should I open first?
faq.a: Open the category of the product you are listing. If you sell more than one kind of item, finish this one, then open the next category.

faq.q: How is a category page different from the template library?
faq.a: These pages group ideas by what you sell. The template library groups them by layout, such as someone wearing the item or a white background. Open a category to see the ideas, then a template to make that layout.

faq.q: Can I begin with a phone photo?
faq.a: Yes. Use one clear photo with the whole item visible. Daylight and a plain surface make the color and the shape easier to check.

faq.q: Will the file keep my product's color and shape?
faq.a: The file is built from the photo you upload. Start with a picture that already shows the color and the full shape.

faq.q: Can I publish from the category page?
faq.a: You make the file from the category page, then send it to TikTok, Facebook, or Instagram, or download it. You still set the budget and the audience in the ad account.

steps_h2: How to Make a Product Photo or Video in 3 Steps

The skillet clip comes back with a voice and captions, and an AI avatar already in the frame, ready for you to post.

trust.h2: AI Ads by Industry, for Every Kind of Seller
trust.lead: Whatever you sell, you can open a category and make the ad from a photo you already have.

items.d: A shop can show a mug being filled, then try a second opening while the listing stays up.
Put a short clip of the new serum on the listing before you order a second carton, so you can judge that clip first.
A bakery can show the loaf on the counter with an AI avatar naming the grain.
You can return two openings from a client's tote photo, and the media plan stays with the person who owns the ad account.
Film yourself once at the packing table and save your face and voice, so later products can use that recording while you pack.
Show the one button that exports the report, large enough to read.

related_h2: Make the Ad, or Browse Another Way
related_lead: Start from a link, an AI avatar, or a template, or open the page for each app you post on.
cta_title: Open the Row for Your Item
cta_lead: Make the next ad from the photo already on the listing. Open the category for the item on your desk and see the credit cost first.

reasons.lead: An avatar, a language, the frames, and your logo can ride along with every category you open.

items.t: A Face That Fits the Category
items.d: For a pet brand, pick an AI actor who looks like they live with the dog.
The spoken line can use the language already printed on the product page. A Japanese tea tin can stay in Japanese.

items.t: Get Help When a File Looks Wrong
items.d: Support can open a launch file with you when something looks off, and you decide whether it posts.

items.t: A Tall Clip and a Square Clip
items.d: A throw-blanket clip can be tall at 9:16 for a phone feed and square at 1:1 for a post. Each frame is its own job.

items.t: Download the File When It Finishes
items.d: When the job finishes, the file is waiting in your account to download.

items.t: Your Logo and the Real Color
items.d: Put your logo on the end card and keep the body cream's real color. The spoken line can sound like your shop.

benefits_h2: One Place for the Whole UGC Ad

benefits.t: An Avatar Matched to the Item
benefits.d: Pick an AI avatar who looks right holding a kettle, and let that face say the line about the handle.

benefits.t: A Listing Photo Becomes a Clip
benefits.d: The blender photo on the listing can move into a clip, and you can start without opening a second design tool.

benefits.t: The Offer in the Buyer's Language
benefits.d: If the buyer reads French, type the offer in French so the jacket sizes stay what you sell.

benefits.t: Set the Feeling of the Line
benefits.d: Note that the mug line should feel quiet, like a late kitchen. The AI avatar's delivery follows that note.
Cut the last second off a phone-case clip in the editor. The trim stays with the file.
Captions arrive with the clip. Recolor them toward the honey label so the words stay readable on a bright counter.

more_sections.eyebrow: Start From What You Already Have
more_sections.h2: Everything That Goes Into the Ad
more_sections.lead: You can start from the photo, the link, or the note you already have, and the ad is built in one place.

items.d: A photo of the desk lamp, or two sentences about the shade, can become the still and the clip you publish.

items.t: A Tool That Builds the Whole Ad
items.d: The tool can build the whole ad from a short brief. Say the backpack is for a commute and the first frame should be the strap, and it asks what is still missing.
If a feed ad moves at a speed that fits your soy candle, describe that speed and use your own jar.
Paste the public page for the face oil. Open [URL to video](page:url-to-video) when you want that flow, and the photo on the page becomes the clip.

items.t: AI Avatars Instead of Filming Yourself
items.d: An AI avatar can hold the shampoo and say the line, so you can stay with the orders in front of you. Browse faces on [AI actors](page:ai-actors).

items.t: Your Face on the Next Products
items.d: Save your own face and voice when the brand is you. Later products can use that recording while you stay at the packing table.

more_sections.eyebrow: Skip the Shoot for This Ad
more_sections.h2: AIVideosUGC Next to Hiring a Creator
more_sections.lead: You spend credits instead of a creator's day rate, and a photo you already have is enough to start.

items.d: Upload the photo you took for the listing. That begins the file, whether or not a creator is free.
You watch the file in your account and decide when it is ready to use.
You know each cost before the job starts, so a test can stay on budget. A photo is 24 credits. A video is 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits for 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds.
Run the coffee tin again with the lid off. A fresh set of credits covers that next version.

items.t: The Line Stays as You Typed It
items.d: You type the sentence about the cedar note, and that sentence stays as you typed it.

items.t: Swap the Product, Keep the Scene
items.d: Keep the kitchen counter and change only the soy candle. The same scene takes the new candle.

items.t: One Face for the Whole Line
items.d: Use one AI avatar for the whole lip-balm line, so the face stays steady each time you add a scent.
Make another version with a new first line and compare the two files in your ad account.
The words go out only after you approve them, so the ad carries your phrasing.
Mark the line as slow and calm, and the next run uses that slower delivery.

reviews.h2: How a Shop Uses Its Industry Page
reviews.lead: Each seller opens the row that matches the item, then makes one clip from a photo they already have.

items.d: They open the beauty row and turn one jar photo into a creator-style clip. The file goes on the product page after they check the color.
They open the clothing row and make a clip of the piece being worn. They post that file instead of booking a fitting day.
They open the tech row and have an AI actor point at one feature of the device. The clip replaces a studio afternoon.
They open the food row and make a pour from the jar they already shot. That clip is the one they run in the feed.

closing.h2: Pick a Plan for This Month
paras: Pick Starter, Pro, or Premium for how many products you launch this month. You see each job's credit cost before it starts.
If a job fails, those credits return. You keep a finished file.
